project.title: A Pharmacy Screen Should Never Be Half Ready
project.subtitle: One owner for loading, readiness, and submission
project.author: Christine John

format.visualDirection: Warm off-white canvas, white surfaces, Bark typography, Oracle red accents, and restrained green, blue, and gold workflow states

big-picture.title: A Pharmacy screen should never be half ready.
big-picture.subtitle: The form and its action must agree about whether the required data is complete.
big-picture.missing: Required task data is still loading

concrete-example.title: The button could trust partial state.
concrete-example.subtitle: Pick Up stored related facts separately, then enabled Submit from only two of them.
concrete-example.gap: This does not prove the latest complete task response is ready.

root-cause.title: The issue is ownership, not the state library.
root-cause.subtitle: Several independent values can tell the screen different stories at the same time.
facts: Latest request is still in flight

one-owner.title: One owner. Three plain questions.
one-owner.subtitle: The open task has one place that can give the UI a consistent answer.

questions.question: Is this task safe to perform?

verify.title: Verify separates rendering from action readiness.
verify.subtitle: The form may render before the Verify button is allowed to act.

fill-dispense.title: Fill has two data gates before its business rules.
fill-dispense.subtitle: Each dependency must be ready in sequence; a partial response cannot enable the action.
fill-dispense.error: Missing action or dispense ID → visible not-ready state

outcome.title: Loading, ready, or recoverable—never half ready.
outcome.subtitle: The button is enabled only when the workflow can actually complete.
outcome.credit: Architecture and narrative direction: Christine John
outcome.sources: Grounded in PR 966 · RX-17230 · pharmacy-ui branch diff
